rationale: Without exact tiny-instance ground truth, every surrogate risks drifting away from the verifier semantics.
first_step: Encode 2-layer and 3-layer constructible grids with a tiny slope alphabet into SAT or MaxSAT and log satisfiable motifs plus UNSAT cores.
expected_signal: Either the first exact nontrivial certificates appear, or the UNSAT cores expose the local motifs that any successful approach must break.

rationale: Hypergraph-bootstrap literature suggests running time can reveal sparse highly reusable dependency structures that pure score search would miss.
first_step: Derive approximate dependency hypergraphs from exact local proofs and rank candidate graphs by closure time at fixed edge-plus-seed budget.
expected_signal: A positive correlation between long infection time and lower score, justifying deeper search in sparse slow families.

rationale: Current sum-difference progress points to bounded-slope and rational-complexity structure as a likely bottleneck.
first_step: Implement a slope scheduler that only unlocks higher-complexity vectors when the low-complexity quotient-module CA has reached a verified fixed point.
expected_signal: Better reuse of local identities, fewer dead-end branches, and smaller slope alphabets at the same verifier success rate.

rationale: The search space is too rugged for single-trajectory optimization, but exact verification makes a diversity archive scientifically meaningful.

expected_signal: Novel certificate families appear in descriptor cells untouched by greedy or annealing baselines, even before the best score improves.
